events.title: A Christmas Carol Published
events.description: Charles Dickens published his novella A Christmas Carol in London, with illustrations by John Leech. The first edition sold out by Christmas Eve.
events.significance: The story helped shape modern Christmas traditions and themes of generosity and social responsibility, and it remains one of the most adapted works in English literature.

events.title: Continental Army Enters Valley Forge
events.description: George Washington led the Continental Army into winter quarters at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania, after campaigns around Philadelphia. Soldiers endured severe shortages of food, clothing, and shelter over the winter.
events.significance: The encampment became a symbol of American perseverance. Training under Baron von Steuben transformed the army into a more disciplined and effective fighting force.

events.title: U.S. House Impeaches President Bill Clinton
events.description: The House of Representatives approved two articles of impeachment against President Clinton, for perjury and obstruction of justice, related to the Monica Lewinsky investigation.
events.significance: Clinton became only the second U.S. president to be impeached, after Andrew Johnson. The Senate acquitted him in February 1999.

events.title: India Annexes Goa
events.description: Indian forces launched Operation Vijay and took control of Goa, Daman, and Diu from Portugal. The Portuguese governor-general surrendered on December 19 after about two days of fighting.
events.significance: The operation ended roughly 450 years of Portuguese colonial rule in India and completed the removal of European colonial enclaves from the subcontinent.

events.title: Andrei Sakharov Released from Internal Exile
events.description: Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev telephoned physicist and dissident Andrei Sakharov to tell him he could return to Moscow from internal exile in Gorky, where he had been held since 1980.
events.significance: The release signaled the openness of Gorbachev's glasnost policy and marked a turning point in the treatment of Soviet dissidents.
